chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) did not validate the testimony of the 'Sābiq al-Hājj' (the precursor of the pilgrims).

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.سَابِقُ الْحَاجِّ: The precursor of the pilgrims (a specific title/group)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of the Sābiq al-Hājj's testimony in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) is recorded as rejecting the testimony of the 'Sābiq al-Hājj,' a title often attributed to those who completed the Hajj but were suspected of lacking sufficient religious integrity or legal knowledge. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that mere ritual completion does not guarantee the reliability (ʿadālah) required for legal witness, emphasizing the need for deeper spiritual and moral qualification.
